proposed statement: The co-op needs to provide growers with timely payment statements to reduce phone inquiries about payment status
key statement: Growers' statements are made in the spreadsheet, printed and posted or emailed, and reach them about three weeks or more after the month ends, because everything is typed, checked and reconciled first.

proposed statement: The system has a paper-based process for bin tracking that uses cardboard tags that fall off, causing confusion
key statement: How will bins be labelled for scanning? Most bins belong to the growers, some numbered and some not; the co-op lends out about 3,000 of its own bins with numbers burnt in; Precious floated a clip-on plastic barcode tag that comes back to the weighbridge, and the consultant will look into what other packhouses do.

proposed statement: The system has a paper-based process for bin tracking that uses cardboard tags that fall off in the rain
key statement: How will bins be labelled for scanning? Most bins belong to the growers, some numbered and some not; the co-op lends out about 3,000 of its own bins with numbers burnt in; Precious floated a clip-on plastic barcode tag that comes back to the weighbridge, and the consultant will look into what other packhouses do.

proposed statement: The Weybridge gate must work offline to avoid fruit sitting in the sun when trucks wait
key statement: Intake at the weighbridge must keep working without the network and catch up when the link is back; trucks can never be stopped at the gate.

proposed statement: The system must work offline at the Weybridge gate to catch up when the network is restored
key statement: Intake at the weighbridge must keep working without the network and catch up when the link is back; trucks can never be stopped at the gate.

proposed statement: The payment calculation is currently handled in a spreadsheet by Sypho, who manually adjusts advance rates based on board decisions
key statement: The advance payment calculation stays in Sipho's spreadsheet for phase one, because the board changes the rates every season; the new system supplies the deliveries and packout as an export.

proposed statement: The statement must be generated either from the new system or Sypho's spreadsheet, depending on how the advance is calculated
key statement: Do statements come from the new system (with Sipho uploading the advances each month) or stay in the spreadsheet?

proposed statement: The office staff (Johan, Maraichi, Precious, and clerks) can access all grower information except bank details and money
key statement: Roles: the office and management see everything; packhouse staff see deliveries and grading but not bank details or payments; growers see their own. Grower records include ID numbers, bank details, addresses and contact details (personal information under POPIA).

proposed statement: The system must keep records for five years for deliveries and statements, and then flag them for deletion
key statement: The consultant suggested that the system keeps a leaver's records for five years and then flags them for deletion, with the co-op deciding; so far nobody has ever thrown anything away.

proposed statement: The client needs to split one truck's weight across several growers by their number of bins
key statement: One truck can carry several growers' bins (a contractor collects from six or seven small growers); intake splits the truck's net weight across growers by number of bins, and each grower's ticket shows his share. The contractor, paid by the growers directly, needs nothing from the system.

proposed statement: The system must allow the clerk to capture a delivery at the Weybridge in under a minute
key statement: Capturing a delivery should take the clerk under a minute (it takes four to five minutes now, and the queue backs up onto the road).

proposed statement: The system must handle 2,400 bins per day at peak volume
key statement: At the peak, 60 to 70 trucks a day, mostly between 07:00 and 11:00, carrying 6 to 40 bins each; 2,400 bins on the peak day last season and about 1,800 on a normal mid-season day.

proposed statement: The client needs to print a small slip for each grower on the truck
key statement: Intake prints a small slip for each grower on the truck for the driver to take away; the carbon books stay as a fallback if the tablet fails, with a quick way to enter those tickets afterwards.

proposed statement: The client wants to know the cost to add Zitsonga and Afrikaans language support
key statement: Should the grower pages also be in Xitsonga (and perhaps Afrikaans)? English is the minimum, and statements must be in English for the auditors; the consultant will price the translation.

proposed statement: The client needs to handle a tablet that can be used outdoors in dusty conditions
key statement: At the weighbridge, a rugged tablet rather than the PC, with big buttons usable with gloves and a screen readable in the sun; at the tipper, as close to one button as possible.

proposed statement: The client needs to ensure the system can handle 10% annual growth in volume
key statement: Volume is growing: two new members are planting, and navel orchards are being replaced with mandarins (smaller fruit, more cartons per bin); the board's plan is 10% more volume a year for the next five years, though Johan isn't sure it will happen.

proposed statement: The client needs to know the number of bins received per cultivar for the previous day to manage daily operations
key statement: A daily summary for management of the previous day's bins received and packout per cultivar, emailed at 06:00 and on a page Johan can look at, also when he is away.

proposed statement: The client experiences a morning rush at the Weybridge where many users access the system simultaneously
key statement: Up to 162 member growers would use the portal (140 delivered last season; the others can come back any time), and the big farms have several users each (owner, manager, perhaps a bookkeeper), so a few hundred users at most.

proposed statement: The client wants the Weybridge intake system to be live by the 1st of March, 2027, and the grower pages by the end of April
key statement: Weighbridge intake live by 1 March 2027 (first mandarins at the end of March); grower pages by the end of April 2027.

proposed statement: The client has a spreadsheet that contains grower lists with orchard blocks and cultivars, about 600 blocks, some of which are outdated
key statement: The grower list with its orchard blocks and cultivars (about 600 blocks, partly out of date, checked by Marietjie) is brought over from the spreadsheet; last season's deliveries only if cheap, to be decided once the consultant has seen the spreadsheet.

proposed statement: The system must handle the Weybridge intake process with tight timing to meet the March 1st deadline
key statement: The Optisort grader's computer is locked down, its reports are PDFs and touching it would void the support contract, so getting packout data out automatically is uncertain and could slip; if it does, Marietjie keeps typing for a while.

proposed statement: The client prefers to have the system report delivery numbers next to totals for easy comparison with tickets
key statement: A monthly export for Sipho's spreadsheet with totals per grower, per cultivar and per class, with the delivery numbers alongside, not one row per bin.

proposed statement: The client's current spray record process is manual and involves multiple methods including paper, email, and WhatsApp
key statement: Maturity test results from the QC lab are on paper and sent to growers as a WhatsApp photo; spray records arrive by paper, email or WhatsApp and are filed in a lever arch file.

proposed statement: The client wants to have the system ready for the first mandarins in March
key statement: Weighbridge intake live by 1 March 2027 (first mandarins at the end of March); grower pages by the end of April 2027.

proposed statement: The client's current process for handling spray records is inconsistent and requires manual intervention
key statement: If a grower's spray records are missing, the delivery is still accepted but marked not for export, with a warning at the weighbridge and at the tipper scan.

proposed statement: The client wants the packhouse team to have two sessions during the season for the portal
key statement: Training in February with practice days on made-up deliveries: two sessions for the packhouse team (shifts) and one for the office; a short manual with pictures; the consultant on site for the first two mornings of the season.

proposed statement: The system should keep each vehicle's empty weight so the clerk doesn't need the list on the wall
key statement: The system keeps each vehicle's empty weight and warns (not blocks) when it is more than a month old, so the clerk weighs that vehicle out and records the new tare; otherwise a grower can be paid for a heavier trailer.

proposed statement: The system must remind when a tear weight is older than a month
key statement: The system keeps each vehicle's empty weight and warns (not blocks) when it is more than a month old, so the clerk weighs that vehicle out and records the new tare; otherwise a grower can be paid for a heavier trailer.

proposed statement: The system must mark deliveries waiting more than three days as red
key statement: A list of deliveries waiting in the holding area and degreening rooms, oldest first, showing the room, with anything waiting more than three days shown in red.

proposed statement: The system must mark deliveries waiting more than three days as red
key statement: Who records that a delivery has moved into a degreening room, and where is it scanned? Not the forklift driver; perhaps someone at the room doors. The consultant will come back with options.

proposed statement: The Wi-Fi doesn't reach inside the degreening rooms, so an access point needs to be installed there
key statement: A list of deliveries waiting in the holding area and degreening rooms, oldest first, showing the room, with anything waiting more than three days shown in red.

proposed statement: The Wi-Fi doesn't reach inside the degreening rooms, so an access point needs to be installed there
key statement: The Wi-Fi doesn't reach inside the degreening rooms (insulated panel walls); scanning at their doors would need another outdoor access point, about R5,000 to R6,000 with cabling.

proposed statement: The tipper scanner should hold scans for a few minutes if the network drops and send them when it's back
key statement: The consultant proposed that the tipper screen holds its scans when the network drops and sends them when it is back, as at the weighbridge: in load-shedding the packhouse generator takes about 30 seconds to start, the Wi-Fi drops meanwhile, and the access points sometimes take two more minutes to come back.

proposed statement: The system should allow one phone number to belong to more than one grower
key statement: When several growers share one phone (for example the Mathebula family, three grower numbers on one phone), does whoever has the phone see all of them, or does each grower need his own number? Sipho will ask the lawyer member.

proposed statement: When growers share a phone, does whoever has the phone see all of those growers or does each grower need his own number?
key statement: When several growers share one phone (for example the Mathebula family, three grower numbers on one phone), does whoever has the phone see all of them, or does each grower need his own number? Sipho will ask the lawyer member.

proposed statement: Growers currently send crop estimates on paper forms that are followed up by phone calls
key statement: Collecting growers' February crop estimates (bins expected per cultivar, which the board wants before the season; now on paper forms that Marietjie chases) on their page: in phase one if there is time, otherwise next season, priced separately.

proposed statement: Small growers may not use the system, so phone calls won't go down
key statement: If the small growers don't use the portal, the calls won't go down; mitigated by showing it at study group days and with the extension officer, Mister Baloyi, who visits every second week.

proposed statement: The grader is a concern that needs addressing
key statement: If the small growers don't use the portal, the calls won't go down; mitigated by showing it at study group days and with the extension officer, Mister Baloyi, who visits every second week.

proposed statement: The system must be offline for the Weybridge location to avoid downtime
key statement: In the season the grower pages must be up on working days including Saturdays (the packhouse works Saturday mornings in the peak, when growers have time to look); an hour down is acceptable, a day is not. The consultant proposed 06:00 to 18:00, Monday to Saturday, with maintenance at night or out of season.

proposed statement: Grower pages should be available during working hours Monday to Saturday from 6 AM to 6 PM during the season
key statement: In the season the grower pages must be up on working days including Saturdays (the packhouse works Saturday mornings in the peak, when growers have time to look); an hour down is acceptable, a day is not. The consultant proposed 06:00 to 18:00, Monday to Saturday, with maintenance at night or out of season.

proposed statement: The consultant must determine who will handle day-to-day system operations like adding growers and resetting tablets
key statement: Who at the co-op looks after the system day to day (adding growers and clerks, resetting tablets)? Perhaps Marietjie's replacement; Johan will come back on it before training.

proposed statement: The client does not know who will be responsible for day-to-day system management, including adding new growers, clerks, and resetting tablets
